items.summary: Alphabet shares fell more than 13% in a record wipeout of over US$500 billion after the company reported disappointing search and advertising sales. Third-quarter services revenue reached US$96.3 billion, below estimates for US$98.4 billion, while ad growth slowed to its weakest pace in five quarters. Chief business officer Philipp Schindler said AI Mode’s rising popularity hurt results, though he noted plans to add more ads there. The reaction underscores investor concerns about the cost of Google’s AI buildout amid weakening core revenue.
items.title: Alphabet’s AI Spending Weighs on Search as Shares Fall Sharply

items.summary: Apple announced two new packages, AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel, extending its earlier local-and-hosted model approach to speech recognition and decisions. The announcement introduces a choice of engines behind Apple's existing APIs: Parakeet v3 (0.6B), Parakeet Ultra from Moondream, NVIDIA's English-only Parakeet Unified, and Alibaba's Qwen3-ASR in 0.6B and 1.7B sizes. Downloads range roughly from about 250 MB to over 2 GB per engine. The team measured the package with its hear command-line tool on an M4 Max Mac Studio running macOS 27.0.1, reporting word error rates of around 23% or higher on AMI recordings where speakers overlap. Apple cautioned that these numbers come from one machine and a few datasets, so users should measure with their own hardware and audio.
items.title: Apple announces open speech and decision models for Swift developers

items.summary: Hugging Face introduces Mistral Large 4 (aka Le Chonk), an open-weight multimodal model with about 1T total and 49B active parameters. It scores 82% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index vulnerability reproduction test, reportedly outperforming closed frontier models that refuse such tasks.
items.title: Mistral Unveils Le Chonk, a Cybersecurity-Focused Open-Weight Multimodal Model

items.summary: Chipmaker STMicroelectronics raised its forecast for AI data centre revenue in 2026 to about US$1.3 billion (S$1.6 billion), up from more than US$1 billion, after third-quarter profit beat expectations on demand from data centres and satellite operators. Chief executive Jean-Marc Chery said the surge was driven mainly by silicon photonics chips.
items.title: STMicroelectronics Raises Data Centre Revenue Forecast After Strong Q3 Profit

items.summary: Google parent Alphabet reported third-quarter results for July to September, taking in almost $128 billion and earning more than $26 billion. Revenue rose about 25 percent year over year while net income fell nearly $9 billion; earnings per share came to $2.12 against a projected $3.02. As of publication the stock was down about 12 percent, one of its largest post-earnings drops.
items.title: Alphabet posts strong Q3 revenue as Google stock falls on AI search concerns

items.summary: French company Mistral says its refined open-weight model, nicknamed Le Chonk, is now the world’s best for automated coding and cybersecurity, matching or surpassing models from Chinese labs like DeepSeek and Z.ai. The trillion-parameter model was trained on increasingly difficult problems. Pierre Stock, VP of science at Mistral, called it a pivotal moment in global AI leadership.
items.title: Mistral Claims Its Open-Weight AI Model Surpasses China in Coding and Cybersecurity

items.summary: Anonymous sources told the New York Times that Alice Huang, a top executive of Singapore's Megaspeed accused in 2025 of reselling restricted Nvidia chips to China, may have acted as a spy by gathering information about Jensen Huang. U.S. intelligence agencies reportedly surveilled her for about a year. An Nvidia spokesperson denied any unusual relationship with the CEO.
items.title: U.S. Investigation Into Possible Chinese Spy Ties at Nvidia

items.summary: In Fast Company's AI Decoded newsletter, senior writer Mark Sullivan questions whether retail investors understand what they are buying in Anthropic's initial public offering. The company filed to raise up to $100 billion, with as much as 20% of shares possibly reserved for retail buyers. Analyst Harrison Rolfes of PitchBook says 'Retail investors buy the story, not the model,' pointing to $11. 6 billion in quarterly revenue against $8. 9 billion spent on compute and more than $430 billion in non-cancelable contracts. Anthropic's S-1 implies an 85% gross margin, but Rolfes notes only 'about 45 cents of each revenue dollar is left' after compute costs.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO May Sell Investors a Story, Not Just Revenue

items.summary: Researchers working with online travel agency Booking.com explored two techniques — knowledge distillation and Medusa, a framework that predicts multiple tokens in parallel at inference time — to make large language models faster and cheaper for real-time travel features. They applied the combined approach across three use cases: an AI Trip Planner, Smart Filters, and accommodation description generation. The final model matched the quality of a 70-billion-parameter teacher while running up to 20 times as fast. Reported outcomes include a 2.9% increase in user engagement for trip planning versus GPT-3.5, responses that were 15 times faster for 99 percent of Smart Filters queries, and 1.4% more helpful ratings on accommodation descriptions at less than one-third the cost of GPT-4.
items.title: Booking.com partners with researchers to speed up travel AI models

items.summary: Meta describes deploying a system it calls Catching Just-in-Time Tests (JiTTests), which uses large language models to generate executable tests that catch bugs before code changes reach production. The company states the approach is now part of its infrastructure rather than a research prototype, and notes engineers have engaged with it at 589 people representing 64% of outreach as of writing. It reports a 60% true-positive rate among reported findings. For the first half of 2026, Meta says Catching JiTTests played a key role in catching 74 serious privacy bugs before they landed and lowered overall occurrences of such privacy issues by 20% during that period.
items.title: Meta Deploys Human-on-the-Loop Bug Catching at Scale

items.summary: Microsoft says it has fixed a problem that blocked non-admin users from connecting via Remote Desktop when the Administrator protection feature is enabled, which prompts authentication before registry or app changes. The failure appeared as error 0xC000000D after installing KB5124010 and later updates on Windows 11 24H2 systems. Microsoft acknowledged the issue on October 13 and says it was resolved by updates released October 28, 2026 (KB5127936) and later. A temporary workaround lets administrators disable admin protection via Intune or Group Policy until next month's Patch Tuesday.
items.title: Microsoft Patches Remote Desktop Failures From Windows Updates

items.summary: Ahead of the holiday season, Amazon added more than 100 new shopping-related capabilities to Alexa for managing subscriptions and lists, updating delivery instructions, solving payment issues, and answering Prime questions. The company said agentic feature users grew 8x year-to-date, with over 400 million consumers using Alexa for shopping in the last 12 months.
items.title: Amazon Expands Alexa Shopping Features Before Holidays

items.summary: French AI lab Mistral released the weights for its trillion-parameter model, Mistral Large 4 (ML4), nicknamed Le Chonk. On the agentic coding benchmark Terminal-Bench 4.0, ML4 scored 41%, up from 28% in preview and beating Opencode's GLM-5.3 by one point. Overall it trails GLM-5.3 at 48 to 49, though Mistral says the model uses 47% fewer tokens per task on average.
items.title: Mistral Ships ML4 'Le Chonk' as Top Open Coding Model

items.summary: Lab COSMO at EPFL evaluated whether low-precision NVIDIA Tensor Core methods can accelerate machine learning interatomic potentials without retraining or changing model architecture. On Blackwell GPUs, cuBLAS's BF16x9 method accelerated major GEMMs by up to 2.5x and the full molecular dynamics step by up to 1.7x on a B300 GPU. Their TF32x3 implementation for Ampere A100 GPUs accelerated major GEMMs by approximately 1.7–1.9x and the complete MD step by up to 1.5x while preserving potential-energy smoothness, energy conservation, and convergence behavior close to the FP32 baseline.
items.title: EPFL Evaluates Tensor Core FP32 Methods for MLIP Inference

items.summary: On the 70th anniversary of the IBM Research Lab in Zurich, Alessandro Curioni — who took over lab leadership more than 10 years ago and now leads its Algorithms and Applications efforts — discussed how he came to stay and his outlook for computing. The interview recounts his path from a physics Nobel announcement as a high school student to pursuing Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics at the Zurich lab, which he described as one of only two places worldwide doing such work. Curioni highlighted talent retention and global collaboration as drivers of success, framed algorithms combining classical, quantum, and AI computing across five problem classes as foundational, and said his dream is creating accurate digital twins of the world in science and business.
items.title: Curioni on IBM Research’s Algorithm Vision at Its 70th Anniversary

items.summary: At Databricks, serverless compute usage has grown more than 3x in the past year as thousands of customers run mission-critical notebooks, jobs, and pipelines on it. To help platform teams gain visibility into rising costs, Databricks is extending cost-control functionality from SQL and Model Serving to all serverless workloads through three capabilities: tags for attribution via system tables, budgets and alerts for monitoring across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, and access controls that let admins govern who can run serverless. Rate limits are also arriving in Beta to cap spend per compute object. Attribution improves at the same time with a new serverless_compute_id field.
items.title: Databricks Brings Serverless Cost Controls to Notebooks, Jobs and Pipelines

items.summary: In a forum post, Yeow Beng Zhen reflects on whether Singaporeans have become too busy to be kind. He suggests the issue is not inherent unkindness but time and emotional strain from work, childcare and caregiving duties. Citing the National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre's National Giving Study 2025, he notes these responsibilities shape volunteering participation. He argues efficiency and kindness need not compete.
items.title: Singaporeans May Be Too Busy To Show Kindness

items.summary: In a forum post, Goh Ee Ca argues that shopping malls should be required to set up dedicated recycling corners for Beverage Container Return Scheme (BCRS) machines. She points to Westgate and IMM as examples where a single supermarket's machine serves all the restaurants in the mall. The author contends it is illogical for members of the public with one or two cans to queue behind commercial operators carrying four large bags, each holding about 100 cans.
items.title: Forum member urges malls to install BCRS recycling corners

items.summary: NVIDIA's GeForce NOW service is adding new cloud gaming titles this Halloween week, headlined by S-GAME's Phantom Blade Zero launching today. The action game features wuxia storytelling with Unreal Engine 5 graphics and over 30 primary weapons. Also arriving Wednesday is World of Warcraft: Forever for eligible members, plus nine additional games joining the library along with mod support for Cyberpunk 2077 and The Witcher 3 Remastered. Ultimate members can access RTX 5080-class performance across multiple devices while GeForce NOW handles downloads and storage without local installs.
items.title: GeForce NOW Adds Phantom Blade Zero and World of Warcraft Forever This Week

items.summary: Roberta Braga of the Digital Democracy Institute of the Americas (DDIA) presents new polling of 1,500 US Latino registered voters suggesting Americans see progress and regulation as compatible. Nearly eight in ten respondents (78%) believe there is a pressing need for stricter rules and oversight of AI, with support spanning Democrats at 83%, Independents at 73%, and Republicans at 72%. Voters worry about job losses, personal data, and unclear AI content while distrusting technology CEOs. Braga argues policy should require risk assessments before powerful systems are released and call for meaningful public participation in infrastructure decisions rather than the familiar innovation-versus-regulation framing.
items.title: Latino Voters Favor AI Oversight Over Unchecked Innovation

items.summary: Mistral AI released Mistral Large 4, nicknamed Le Chonk, an improved open-weight multimodal model trained from scratch on European infrastructure. The update emphasizes coding and defensive cybersecurity gains after three weeks of reinforcement learning since its public preview. It leads FrontierCode with a score of 19.7% and scores 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index while refusing malicious requests at a rate of 96.6%. Pricing starts at $0.70 input per million tokens, output at $2.10. Partners La Banque Postale and Microsoft Foundry support its deployment for sovereign AI use cases.
items.title: Mistral Releases Improved Open-Weight Le Chonk Model

items.summary: Will Orr argues that current training dataset transparency mandates fail to deliver meaningful accountability for large language models. While California and the European Union require companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI and Meta to publish high-level summaries of their datasets, these disclosures describe only what is included rather than why it was chosen or how decisions were made. Orr calls such statements 'transparency theater' that amounts to performative compliance, noting they hide consequential choices about web crawling, data cleaning and quality benchmarks like Hellaswag. He urges regulators to require companies to disclose their criteria, maintain version logs of decision rationales and open pipelines to independent auditors rather than limiting scrutiny to copyright litigation.
items.title: Why AI Training Dataset Transparency Mandates Fall Short

items.summary: Aditya Chakrabortty, the Guardian's senior economics correspondent who received an MBE earlier this year for public understanding of the economy, will host a Reader Q&A. He is online at 2pm GMT (9am EDT) on Friday 30 October to answer questions about economics and politics. Readers can email conversations@theguardian.com or sign up from 8am GMT.
items.title: Guardian economist Aditya Chakrabortty hosts reader Q&A on economics and politics

items.summary: Sterling Anderson, the former Tesla Autopilot director now GM's chief product officer, called dropping radar for a camera-only self-driving system “a weird religious stance that ignores physics.” Speaking to The Verge on October 27, he said scaling back to vision-only risks trouble in certain situations and that cameras cannot see through dense fog or measure instantaneous velocity like radar. His remarks arrive as Tesla pushes driverless Cybercabs in Austin while NHTSA investigates FSD camera degradation across 3,203,754 vehicles after nine crashes. Anderson's GM roadmap favors lidar, radar, and cameras over vision-only.
items.title: Ex-Tesla Autopilot Head Criticizes Vision-Only Self-Driving as Physics-Ignoring

items.summary: Finnish police have launched a criminal investigation into possible breaches of environmental law at the site of a planned Google datacentre in northern Finland. Authorities allege that Tuike Finland, a Google subsidiary, cleared and drained 330 hectares (815 acres) of forest before required impact assessments were completed. Google’s country manager has apologised but said it acted on its understanding of the law at the time.
items.title: Finland Opens Criminal Probe Into Google Datacentre Forest Clearing

items.summary: The US filed a lawsuit in Manhattan federal court accusing Google of failing to reemploy Mark Davisson after his year of military leave as a US Army reservist. The complaint, filed Thursday (Oct 29), says the employee spent two years as a key account executive handling accounts for BlackRock, Bridgewater Associates and Credit Suisse before returning in May 2023. Google allegedly barred him from customer accounts while he kept his pay and title, then assigned him to a cloud solutions role with no client management duties before firing him in August 2024 amid workforce reductions.
items.title: US Sues Google Over Reservist Reemployment

items.summary: The euro edged up roughly 0. 11% against the dollar after the ECB kept interest rates unchanged, though it warned inflation risks were rising from surging energy costs and announced Christine Lagarde would step down in February rather than October 2027. The move followed US data showing September inflation accelerated as consumers paid more for gasoline, supporting expectations of a December rate hike by the Federal Reserve, which had delayed changes until after midterm elections.
items.title: ECB Holds Rates as Euro Gains on US Inflation Data

items.summary: Google has launched Gemini 4 Carbon, an artificial intelligence model built for coding and cybersecurity tasks such as finding hidden software weaknesses. The company says it scored 88.2% on the SEC-bench Pro test without safety guardrails, though Google notes real-world performance is not guaranteed. Access currently goes only to selected cybersecurity experts due to misuse concerns; pricing starts at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
items.title: Google Launches Restricted Gemini 4 Carbon AI Model

items.summary: The European Central Bank announced on Wednesday that President Christine Lagarde will step down from the job in February, eight months before her tenure was set to end. The decision sets up a leadership contest at the bank as Europe faces major inflationary pressures, largely sparked by the war in Iran.
items.title: ECB Chief Lagarde To Step Down In February

items.summary: Microsoft is raising at least $25 billion in its first U.S. bond sale since 2017, split into 10 series of notes with two floating-rate and eight fixed-rate tranches. The document leaves principal amounts, interest rates and maturity dates blank, though maturities range from two to 40 years. J.P. Morgan, UBS Investment Bank and Wells Fargo Securities are joint book-running managers. Net proceeds may fund working capital, capex, buybacks, acquisitions or debt repayment.
items.title: Microsoft Plans $25 Billion Bond Sale After 2017

items.summary: Apple describes touch gestures available on its new PROLED XDR display, which houses a built-in touch sensor. A finger slide scrolls pages or documents; pinching zooms photos and content. Double-tapping expands windows while flicking tiles them into place. The system also supports sketching, annotation, 3D prototype manipulation, music controls, and third-party apps like Algoriddim djay Pro. Touch works alongside keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures.
items.title: Apple Explains Touch Gestures on New MacBook Pro Display

items.summary: American automakers reported third quarter earnings showing rising revenues but mounting production costs from tariffs on steel, aluminum and copper; higher diesel prices around $6.35 a gallon; and pricier computer chips amid supply-chain tightness. General Motors projected materials, chip and diesel costs could reach about $2 billion this year, while Ford expects commodities, memory and logistics to add roughly $2 billion in headwind. Customers kept buying vehicles despite affordability concerns, with the average new vehicle transaction price near a record high above $50,000. The electric transition weakened after the federal EV tax credit ended Sept. 30, 2025, but hybrid sales rose about 27% as fuel prices stayed elevated.
items.title: American Automakers Face Rising Costs From Tariffs, Diesel and Chips

items.summary: The WTO's Global Review 2026 focuses on partnerships advancing trade and development, noting that USD 795 billion in Aid for Trade investments has helped developing economies build infrastructure, skills and institutions. DG Okonjo-Iweala observed African economies' export shares remain around 3 and 1 per cent, while the OECD-WTO report shows developing economies now account for nearly half of global merchandise exports, up from 38 per cent in 2006. The Review features plenaries, regional spotlights and member-led sessions on topics including digital trade and artificial intelligence.
items.title: WTO Global Review Highlights Aid for Trade Partnerships

items.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's President Ouattara, speaking in the WTO Presidential Lecture Series, described re-globalization—broader, more resilient and inclusive globalization—as a chance to shift developing economies from raw-material exports toward value creation. He cited Côte d'Ivoire's average economic growth of 7 per cent between 2012 and 2025 as evidence. Director-General Okonjo-Iweala noted trade-system uncertainty but called African countries' recent high growth promising, stressing that national reforms must be complemented by changes at the WTO.
items.title: Ivorian President Frames Re-globalization as Path Beyond Raw-Commodity Trade

items.summary: The Trump administration pledged tariff relief to automakers that commit to building in the U.S., as it negotiated a $4 billion Audi Georgia plant, per The Wall Street Journal. Audi executives sought a break and were assured by the Commerce Department of a new program likely using exemptions or offsets. Companies must promise to begin construction to qualify; specifics remain being finalized.
items.title: Trump Administration Offers Tariff Relief Tied to U.S. Auto Investment

items.summary: Columnist Faisal Islam argues Jeremy Healey's Budget was deliberately small rather than a mini-Budget. It fell short of the promised new economic model and unveiled no growth theory as Prime Minister Andy Burnham had pledged. The move aimed to avoid market shock after Liz Truss's fiscal event, achieving only modest breathing space for households and government amid energy pressures, welfare cost rises projected at £431bn by 2031, and a defence target of 3% of national income by 2030.
items.title: Islam calls Healey's Budget a deliberate 'micro' event, not radical reform

items.summary: US intelligence agencies reportedly believe Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, has been targeted by a Chinese spy who had done business with him. The New York Times reported that Alice Huang of Megaspeed was suspected of smuggling chips and acting as an intelligence asset. White House officials are reportedly alarmed by her access to the CEO. Nvidia stated there was nothing out of the ordinary about their interactions.
items.title: Nvidia Chief Executive Reported Targeted by Chinese Spy

items.summary: A 2026 study by ecologist Natalia Camps Pimenta and colleagues reports that Baniwa fishers along the Içana River in Brazil’s Upper Rio Negro coexist with giant otters rather than conflict over them. In interviews, 84% of 19 fishers said they regularly encounter otters during the dry season, yet only 32% view them as competitors. The researchers attribute this to spatial and dietary separation, behavioral adaptation such as moving fishing spots or reducing noise, historical fur-trade persecution from the mid-1900s that may have made otters wary of people, and Baniwa cosmology in which otters are spiritual guardians of fish. Pimenta told Mongabay that coexistence reflects a combination of cultural values, market demand, external pressure and environmental diversity, and she hopes conservation will recognize Indigenous knowledge as a sophisticated management system rather than merely supplementary information.
items.title: Baniwa Fishers and Otters Share Amazon Rivers in Coexistence

items.summary: ECB president Christine Lagarde said Thursday she is leaving the European Central Bank early, stepping down on 7 February 2027, around nine months before her term would have ended. She told reporters in Frankfurt that the neutrality expected of central bankers was no longer something she could accept and added “Whether people will listen or not is another story. ” The ECB left its deposit rate unchanged at 2. 5%, but Lagarde said policymakers had debated a hike, with the pause possibly lasting only until December. Eurozone inflation rose to 3. 8% in September, energy prices up 18. 9% year on year, and she noted the average 10-year government bond yield had risen around 35 basis points since September’s projections. French borrowing costs eased Thursday to about 4. 88%, still roughly 154 basis points above Germany’s.
items.title: Lagarde Cites Loss of Neutrality in Early ECB Departure

items.summary: A “super El Niño” has driven reduced rainfall across Roraima, drying up the seasonal Véu de Noiva waterfall in Serra Grande before its usual end. Fábio Wankler of UFRR attributes the disruption to unusually intense weather shifts causing longer droughts. Owner Ivaldo Araújo reported tourist numbers fell by half after only three months of rain, an estimated loss of about $500,000 Brazilian Reais — around $100,000. Guide Fredson Guedes lost income and adapted to beaches and hikes. The Roraima government declared a state of emergency in early September 2026 with an 180-day decree. NOAA says the El Niño has a 75% chance of becoming the most intense on record since 1950, with effects projected into early 2027.
items.title: El Niño ends Roraima waterfall season early, hurting tourism

items.summary: The French AI company Mistral has released the weights of its Large 4 (ML4) model, nicknamed “Le Chonk”, positioning it as a coding and cyber-defence tool that organisations can run on their own infrastructure. The firm claims ML4 is the best open agentic coding model in the world and offers frontier cyber-defence capabilities for detecting, analysing and responding to threats across code and IT systems. Mistral says its Terminal-Bench 4.0 score rose from 28% to 41%, and that it uses 47% fewer tokens per task than Chinese model GLM-5.3. The release is framed as part of Europe’s effort to build alternatives to US and Chinese technology amid growing dependence concerns, though the model relies on Nvidia chips trained at Mistral’s European data centres.
items.title: Mistral Releases Open Cyber-Defence AI Model for Download

items.summary: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announced her resignation on Thursday, ending months of speculation about her future. She will step down Feb. 7, giving EU leaders time to choose a successor before the French presidential election that polls favor far-right candidate Marine Le Pen. The move comes as the ECB faces inflation risks from an Iran-driven oil shock and rising bond yields threatening growth.
items.title: ECB President Lagarde Resigns Amid Rising Economic and Political Challenges for Europe

items.summary: Christine Lagarde announced she is stepping down from her role as European Central Bank president on 7 February 2027, before the end of her term. The ECB said she informed its governing council and European Council president Antonio Costa of the decision. No reason has been given for the early departure, though speculation links it to upcoming French elections that could affect successor selection.
items.title: ECB President Lagarde Announces Premature Departure in February

items.summary: The European Central Bank announced that its president, Christine Lagarde, will step down on February 7, 2027, nearly nine months before her term expires. Her successor will be appointed by the European Council under EU treaty rules. The early departure opens a window for leaders to name a new chief ahead of French elections in April. Officials praised her stewardship through the pandemic and inflation shocks, with succession preparations set to begin immediately. Lagarde has ruled out standing for re-election, citing it as not advisable.
items.title: ECB President Lagarde Announces Departure in February 2027

items.summary: A CGTN commentator, Xu Ying, argues that the second season of the drama VIVANT distorts historical memory by placing torture methods tied to Imperial Japan's wartime atrocities in China into the hands of Chinese characters. She contends scenes depicting mutilation and bayonet attacks have a documented provenance: war criminal Gisaburo Ikeda confessed to killing civilians with bayonets, and Kiyoshi Kawashima testified about victims' suffering. The commentator asserts that reversing perpetrators and victims reverses moral positions and risks reinforcing misconceptions. Responding to the defense that fiction differs from fact, she calls for production teams to explain their research, broadcasters to strengthen historical consultation, and political figures to exercise care in endorsements. She frames Germany's post-war reckoning as a model of acknowledging responsibility rather than shifting it. The piece is an opinion column reflecting the author's views, not necessarily CGTN's official position.
items.title: CGTN Commentator Criticizes VIVANT Drama for Distorting Japan's Wartime Atrocities

items.summary: Song Yuehong, a CGTN commentator and research fellow at the Institute of Contemporary China Studies, explains principles from the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, which concluded in Beijing on October 29. The meeting adopted a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, emphasizing serving missions, political strengthening as an overarching principle, comprehensive coverage, rigor, problem orientation, top-down approach, and rule-based governance. Yuehong argues that confining power within institutional frameworks is central to this effort, which aims to strengthen the Party's mission sense, unity, integrity, and leadership while advancing Chinese modernization through improved systems for self-governance.
items.title: CGTN Commentator Outlines Party Self-Governance Principles

items.summary: Governor Mike Dunleavy ordered an investigation into a scheme that led two men named Dan Sullivan onto Alaska's US Senate ballot in the midterm elections. He said he was responding to New York Times reporting alleging Peltola campaign and Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee staff tried to recruit spoiler candidates, though the BBC has not independently verified the report. The incumbent Republican senator and allies accuse Democrats of confusing voters; Peltola's team deny wrongdoing. Analysts call it one of the tightest races nationally.
items.title: Alaska Governor Orders Probe Into Same-Name Candidate Scheme

items.summary: The United States and Japan agreed Wednesday night in Cebu, Philippines, to build a Japanese facility for the joint production of advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles. The announcement was made by Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi at an annual meeting of Southeast Asian defense chiefs alongside U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. He said the Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile, produced under a program called Operation Supercharge, is essential for F-35 fighter jets and that both sides agreed to strengthen deterrence with greater speed than before. Koizumi also raised concern about China's increasing naval activity in southwestern Japan this week.
items.title: US and Japan Agree on Missile Production Facility

items.summary: China's top leaders elevated Gen. Zhang Shengmin, the last remaining general on the Central Military Commission besides Xi Jinping, to the Politburo during a four-day closed-door meeting. They also adopted a resolution strengthening self-governance, discipline and anti-corruption as they seek to extend their grip on power ahead of President Xi's expected fourth term in 2012. Analyst Neil Thomas noted attendance at just 74 percent, the lowest since Mao Zedong.
items.title: Chinese Leaders Elevate Military General and Reinforce Party Discipline

items.summary: Partial results from Israel's general election show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu marginally ahead of rival Gadi Eisenkot, but still short of a parliamentary majority. With 99% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies were on track for 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, while Eisenkot's bloc was set for 48; both leaders say they will try to form a coalition. Arab-led parties could win an unprecedented 19 seats as potential kingmakers, though most Jewish parties have pledged not to work with them. President Isaac Herzog is expected to consult factions next week and invite the leader he judges best placed to govern, warning of another election if talks fail.
items.title: Israel election results leave Netanyahu's bloc short of a majority

items.summary: The US filed a lawsuit accusing Google of failing to restore an employee, Mark Davisson, to his former role or provide a comparable position after he returned from military leave as a US Army reservist. The complaint alleges that upon his return in May 2023, the company restricted him from managing customer accounts before firing him in August 2024 amid workforce reductions. Google did not immediately respond to comment requests.
items.title: US Sues Google Over Reservist's Job Loss

items.summary:
The Supreme Court pulled up the Reserve Bank of India on Thursday, directing banks to compensate victims when their own employees are involved in cyberfrauds. A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant questioned why banks should not be held accountable for customer losses they can waive through one-time settlements worth ₹5 crore or ₹10 crore. Attorney General R. Venkataramani opposed the rule, arguing liability must fall on RBI instead. The court granted time till 30 November to file proposed amendment directions. A Hindustan Times report cited over 21,900 complaints involving ₹647 crore in eight months of 2026, while Venkataramani said digital arrest cases fell about 50% from last year.

visual:null,
items.title: Supreme Court Pressures RBI Over Bank Liability in Cyberfraud Cases

items.summary: Christine Lagarde arrived at the European Central Bank in 2019 as its first chief without formal economics training or central banking experience, prompting some market participants to call her a 'credibility risk.' She later acknowledged she had expected only a five-year mandate. After navigating a pandemic, energy shocks and severe euro zone inflation, critics like economist Willem Buiter credited her with bringing inflation down faster than peers in Britain and the United States, while others, including Paul De Grauwe, dismissed her as politically driven. Her departure on February 7 leaves successors facing strained French bond markets and renewed inflation risks.
items.title: Christine Lagarde's ECB Tenure Defied Sceptics Despite Political Roots

items.summary: Israel's Shin Bet is investigating suspicions that Qatar and Turkey funneled money to sway Arab voters in the pivotal polls, per a Central Elections Committee order from chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg. The inquiry follows reports the agency held intelligence before elections but did not share it; investigators caution 'this is not a drama.' Qatar denies interference, while Likud alleges election theft and Arab leaders reject those claims as politically motivated.
items.title: Shin Bet probe into alleged foreign election funding

items.summary: Chennai police briefly detained economist A Kalaiyarasan over an allegedly abusive Instagram comment about Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam MLA J Kamatchi posted by a fake account using his photograph. Kalaiyarasan alleged officers arrived at his home around 5 am without documents and denied having the account, suspecting his photo came from Harvard University. Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam chief MK Stalin condemned the action as fascism.
items.title: Chennai Police Detain Economist Over Fake Instagram Account Using His Photo

items.summary: French startup Mistral released its Large 4 model publicly on Thursday, describing it as an upgrade from the version unveiled three weeks earlier. Unlike Google's Gemini, which relies on online services, the model can be downloaded and run independently. Mistral Vice President of Science Pierre Stock said open weights are essential once a model is out.
items.title: Mistral AI Releases Large 4 Model for Cybersecurity Users

items.summary: Tamil Nadu police detained Assistant Professor A Kalaiyarasan of the Madras Institute of Development Studies at dawn on Wednesday, Oct 29, allegedly over an abusive comment from a fake Instagram account using his photograph. Police later released him three hours after confirming his photo had been misused to create the account @youvijayamani. DMK president M K Stalin condemned the detention as 'peak of fascism' and demanded an apology from police and Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, while CPI (M) leader P Shanmugam urged a proper inquiry into who created the account.
items.title: Economist Kalaiyarasan Detained Over Fake Instagram Post; Stalin Condemns TVK Action

items.summary: The US Department of Justice is reportedly questioning Nvidia over its $12.93 billion deal to buy the open-source platform Hugging Face, two people familiar with the matter said. The inquiry examines whether the acquisition would let Nvidia capture a key AI distribution point and harm rivals, running alongside years-long investigations into Nvidia's broader conduct that began under President Biden and continue under President Trump. Two DOJ officials cautioned that government probes are not evidence of wrongdoing and may lead to no action. Nvidia declined comment; Hugging Face did not respond. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027, per Nvidia.
items.title: DOJ Inquiry Into Nvidia's Hugging Face Purchase

items.summary:
Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday that the details of the India-US trade deal, when made public, would show India had safeguarded farmers' interests while securing a strong comparative advantage. Speaking at the fourth National Conference on India's Industrial Transformation in New Delhi, he noted nine free trade agreements have opened markets with combined GDP of $60 trillion versus $10 trillion before 2014. Goyal also defended withdrawing from RCEP and projected India’s space economy could grow to $44 billion by 2033. He attributed long-term growth to talent, skills and energy over the next 20-25 years.

items.summary: The Supreme Court said it was not inclined to impose a complete ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, but warned authorities against failing to enforce its orders. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale stressed that air pollution affects every living being and that repeated directions serve little purpose without ground-level compliance. The court called for cooperation from all stakeholders.
items.title: Supreme Court Warns Delhi Authorities Over Firecracker Enforcement

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar dismissed the legislative council election results after the Samajwadi Party defeated the Bharatiya Janata Party in the Varanasi Graduates' constituency. He said the outcome reflected a mandate from educated voters rather than the general electorate, playing down their significance.
items.title: UP Minister Downplays MLC Election Results as Educated-Voter Mandate

items.summary: Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday that India would have a strong comparative advantage in the free trade agreement being negotiated with the United States, stressing that no farmers' interests or sensitive sectors would be compromised. Speaking at the 4th ISID-IDRA National Conference on India's Industrial Transformation, he added that Indians would celebrate once details are released and described eight FTAs finalised by the Modi government as finding no single flaw. External affairs minister S Jaishankar said last week the deal is in its 'last mile' but noted it is never done till it's done.
items.title: Goyal says India has comparative edge in US trade deal
